lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Lakeside Golf Club | Caddie | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Caddied about 5 rounds a week, carrying bags and reading greens for members.
- Helped the pro shop run the weekend junior tournament.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved close efficiency by 40% by automating reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Wrote the variance commentary for the monthly board pack, explaining each line more than 5% off budget.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Reported a 45% group EBITDA margin by adding the EBITDA margins of the three business units.
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Underwrote 60 small-business loans worth USD 45M, and none of the approved loans defaulted in their first two years.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Tested the valuation's sensitivity: a 1-point change in the discount rate moved the share value from USD 52 to USD 44.
- Shared the model and a two-page note with the university investment club, which used it in its spring pitch.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Built an 18-month cash forecast for a USD 600M business, holding error to about 4% and freeing USD 40M to repay debt early.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Bloomberg Terminal
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: Finance experience should appear before education.
items.because: After five years of post-degree work, leading with the degree makes the résumé feel student-oriented and may hide the most relevant experience.

items.says: The Caddie role should not be the first experience signal.
items.because: Its position gives a finance reader an unrelated first impression despite stronger finance roles elsewhere.

items.says: The Caddie entry should be shortened and visually subordinated.
items.because: Its duties offer little relevant finance evidence and take attention from the analyst and credit roles.

items.says: Projects should follow finance experience.
items.because: That placement would better support the résumé's finance direction.

items.says: The older Student Investment Fund project should be shortened or removed.
items.because: Keeping it prominent weakens the progression and adds material that appears disconnected.

items.says: The caddie bullet gives duties and activity volume but no evidence of effective service.
items.because: The reader cannot see what value the work delivered to members or the club.

items.says: The tournament bullet does not identify the candidate's contribution or its outcome.
items.because: “Helped the pro shop run” leaves the tasks unclear, and the event name gives no measure of scope or success.

items.says: The 40% close-efficiency result lacks a defined metric and prior-process baseline.
items.because: A hiring manager cannot tell what improved by 40% or what supplied the comparison.

items.says: The bullet repeats “by” in a clumsy causal construction.
items.because: The repetition makes the relationship between the result and the automation harder to scan.

items.says: The capital-plan bullet buries the standardization result behind conversational wording.
items.because: “So every request used” describes the purpose instead of directly showing what changed.

items.says: The capital-plan bullet gives no quantified business or decision-making impact.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether the common template improved approvals, comparability, or capital allocation.

items.says: The variance-commentary bullet gives no outcome.
items.because: It shows a recurring responsibility but not how the commentary improved decisions, accountability, forecasts, or board understanding.

items.says: The 5% budget threshold is difficult to parse.
items.because: It is unclear what items were measured and how the threshold was applied.

items.says: The valuation discounts free cash flow to equity at WACC.
items.because: FCFE should generally use the cost of equity; WACC is appropriate for free cash flow to the firm.

items.says: The valuation bullet gives no valuation result or decision impact.
items.because: Without a value or decision, the method overwhelms the accomplishment.

items.says: The group EBITDA margin is calculated by adding business-unit margins.
items.because: Margins cannot be added to produce a group margin; the calculation needs total EBITDA divided by total revenue or a revenue-weighted average.

items.says: The EBITDA-margin bullet gives no resulting management impact.
items.because: It does not show a planning, performance-review, or management decision enabled by the figure.

items.says: The rolling cash-flow forecast bullet should open the Stonebridge entry.
items.because: Its scale, accuracy, and financial consequence make it the strongest opening evidence.

items.says: “Letting treasury pay down” is an informal, weak causal phrase.
items.because: It weakens the connection between the forecast and the debt repayment.

items.says: The underwriting bullet does not state the analytical basis for the loans.
items.because: The reader sees the volume and performance but not the judgment that produced them.

items.says: The no-default result needs a defined observation period or cohort.
items.because: “None of the approved loans defaulted in their first two years” does not define the group observed.

items.says: The approval-rate result is buried.
items.because: The reader must pass the review scope and threshold change before reaching the strongest result.

items.says: The bullet uses the first-person pronoun “my.”
“No rise in early defaults” lacks a baseline or comparison period.
items.because: That omission weakens confidence in the risk-control outcome.

items.says: “Writes” uses the wrong tense for a role that ended in December 2022.
items.because: It makes the responsibility read as though it is ongoing.

items.says: The reduction in missed covenant tests has no defined scope.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether 7 to 1 applies to the whole portfolio or an average period.

items.says: The bullet does not identify the monitoring-process change.
items.because: It does not say whether the checklist added scheduling, escalation, documentation, or another control.

items.says: The spreading-template bullet does not say what the tool automated or standardized.
items.because: The process or technical skill behind cutting memo time from six hours to three is unclear.

items.says: The 6% market-price comparison lacks a defined valuation output and price date.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether it compares an implied share price with a dated market price.

items.says: “A 1-point change” does not specify a percentage-point change or its direction.
items.because: Those details distinguish the rate change from a relative percentage change and explain the move from USD 52 to USD 44.

items.says: The sensitivity bullet opens with a task rather than the quantified result.
items.because: The reader has to wait for the more precise share-price impact.

items.says: “Which used it” refers ambiguously to the model or the note.
items.because: The reader cannot tell which material the club used.

items.says: The bullet does not explain how the materials affected the spring pitch.
items.because: Adoption alone does not show the recommendation, presentation, investment conclusion, or decision enabled.

items.says: The FP&A bullet uses broad, assistance-oriented language.
items.because: “Supported the FP&A team” suggests assistance, while “financial reporting and analysis” is too broad to show the work or relevant skill.

items.says: The FP&A bullet gives no concrete deliverable or result.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what the candidate produced or why it mattered.

items.says: The performance-reporting bullet should lead the Student Investment Fund entry.
items.because: It is the strongest project evidence, but its impact is buried in a trailing clause.

items.says: The report bullet does not say what the committee did differently because of it.
items.because: Frequent use shows adoption but not an investment decision, portfolio action, or monitoring process.

items.says: The cash-forecast accuracy metric is undefined and imprecise.
items.because: “About 4%” does not identify what the error measures or give a precise figure.

items.says: The student-fund bullet duplicates the Stonebridge cash-forecast achievement.
items.because: The two entries repeat the duration, company scale, forecast error, and debt repayment result despite separate dates and settings.

items.says: The forecast bullet does not show how the forecast was constructed.
items.because: It gives the output without showing the forecasting method.

items.says: Bloomberg Terminal appears unsupported.
items.because: No experience or project bullet connects it to market-data, research, or valuation work.
